sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: Very little change in the large-scale upper flow field over the U.S. is expected today, as a low remains in place over the Great Basin vicinity and a ridge persists over the south-central states. Elsewhere, fast west-northwest flow will prevail from the Upper Great Lakes and Midwest region across the Northeast, and a very weak upper disturbance will linger over the Florida vicinity. At the surface, a wavy frontal zone will remain draped from the central Plains region east across the Midwest/Ohio Valley to the Mid-Atlantic Coast. Meanwhile, a cold front crossing southern Nevada/eastern Utah should slow/weaken with time.

sections.title: The Midwest east to the Mid-Atlantic Coast
sections.text: Showers and scattered/elevated thunderstorms are forecast to be ongoing across portions of the risk area at the start of the period, as numerous small-scale disturbances aloft -- embedded with fast west-northwest flow -- advance east-southeastward. One of the more prominent of these disturbances -- now crossing the Iowa vicinity -- should reach Ohio/western Pennsylvania by early afternoon. While lingering clouds/precipitation will likely have hindered heating to some degree, some destabilization near and south of the front -- expected to be lying from central Ohio east to central/southern New Jersey -- should promote development of scattered showers and thunderstorms -- initially from western Pennsylvania into central Ohio. With fast/roughly unidirectional west-southwest flow aloft, storms may organize into one or more fast-moving bands, with damaging winds becoming the primary severe risk. Greatest risk appears likely to occur from south-central and southeast Pennsylvania and northern Maryland to southern New Jersey and northern Delaware. sections.title: Synopsis
sections.text: In mid/upper levels, a split-flow pattern will persist, featuring a large, quasistationary cyclone over the Great Basin that is cut off from a cyclonically curved northern-stream flow belt over central/ eastern Canada. The split belt around the western cyclone moves through a mean ridge over the central/northern Plains, then enters gently confluent, west-northwesterly flow from the Great Lakes across the Mid-Atlantic and New England, effectively rejoining the northern stream. An embedded MCV and associated low-amplitude shortwave trough were evident in satellite and composited radar animations over the IA/IL border region. This perturbation should move east-southeastward, reaching western/central PA around 00Z, then weakening and moving offshore tonight. At the surface, 11Z analysis showed a wavy, quasistationary frontal zone from a low over west-central KS to another low over central IL (this one related to the nearby perturbation aloft), then eastward across central OH and southwestern PA. sections.title: Coastal Mid-Atlantic to Corn Belt
sections.text: Focused low/middle-level lift -- above the surface and related to the MCV, including mass convergence and warm advection -- is contributing to ongoing organized but non-severe thunderstorms over northwestern IL. Disorganized patches of weaker convection are evident in the downshear flow stream from there across southern Lower MI to offshore NJ. All of this activity should reinforce the baroclinic zone across the region, which should move only on minor/localized scales today. This afternoon, scattered thunderstorms should develop near the front over portions of eastern OH and western PA, moving eastward to southeastward into a favorably destabilized, weakly capped air mass toward the coastal Mid-Atlantic. Severe potential should be focused most tightly near the outflow boundary/front. Damaging gusts will be the most common event type, though sporadic hail and a tornado or two are possible as well. Fast-moving bands or clusters of storms should be the dominant modes, though some potential exists for supercells as well. outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms with damaging winds as the primary hazard are most likely across portions of the Upper Ohio Valley to the Mid-Atlantic Coast in the late afternoon and evening.

sections.title: Corn Belt to Mid-Atlantic Coast
sections.text: A pair of MCVs in conjunction with a strong baroclinic zone will be the primary drivers of severe storm development expected to begin in the late afternoon. While the overall synoptic pattern is more typical of mid-late June, boundary-layer moisture is not of summertime quality and will likely mitigate a greater severe weather threat. 12Z NAM soundings appear to have the typical moist bias in increasing mean-mixing ratios well above other guidance such as the RAP, which results in overdone buoyancy profiles at peak heating. Primary severe focus is expected to develop downstream of the remnant MCV currently near the MI/OH/IN border region. Robust diabatic heating south of the surface front that lies from central OH to PA should result in scattered storm development late afternoon from east-central OH across southern PA. The eastern extent of frontal placement near the Mid-Atlantic Coast has lower confidence given an extensive stratus deck that is only slowing eroding across eastern PA and most of NJ. sections.title: Eastern TX Panhandle/Northwest TX vicinity
sections.text: Mean-mixing ratios have increased compared to yesterday's 12Z soundings at Midland, Fort Worth, and Del Rio. Storm coverage is expected to be greater than yesterday along the dryline during the late afternoon to early evening. While upper-level winds will be weak and limit updraft organization, deeply mixed thermodynamic profiles will support a risk for isolated severe wind gusts between about 23-02Z.

sections.title: North-central CO
sections.text: Some guidance suggests a supercell or two may form off the Front Range/Foothills at some point this evening within a low-level upslope flow regime. Pervasive stratus over the plains north of the Palmer Divide will likely limit the spatial extent of the severe risk. Deep-layer shear profiles will be conducive to updraft rotation and the primary hazard should be large hail. ..Grams/Marsh.. 05/12/2018

outlooks.summary: Scattered severe storms with damaging winds as the primary hazard are most likely across portions of the Upper Ohio Valley to the Mid-Atlantic Coast through this evening.

sections.title: Discussion
sections.text: Have opted not to change enhanced risk / 30% wind probabilities with this update. Ahead of a low-amplitude impulse noted over Ohio as of 1930Z, convection has gradually deepened across the upper Ohio Valley this afternoon. Although an 18Z PIT sounding sampled only modest boundary-layer moisture (e.g., 9.7 g/kg mean mixing ratio), increasing buoyancy with eastward extent and steep low-level lapse rates should further enhance the wind threat through this evening, as one or more small bowing segments organize and head towards the coast. Farther west, the slight risk was contracted some over Indiana, essentially to focus the forecast threat to where ascent from an MCV (moving east/southeast over eastern Illinois currently) will eventually intersect a more unstable environment near/south of the front. Over Iowa/Illinois, the marginal risk was focused farther north, as the only remaining threat within the D1 period will likely be isolated hail associated with elevated convection overnight. ..Picca.. 05/12/2018 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1128 AM CDT Sat May 12 2018/

mesoscale_discussions.summary: A severe thunderstorm watch will be needed this afternoon into the evening for parts of central and eastern Ohio to central Pennsylvania, northern West Virginia and the Maryland Panhandle. Strong to severe storms are expected to develop by 3-4 PM EDT across central and eastern Ohio into western Pennsylvania, and spread to the east-southeast producing damaging wind as the primary threat.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Early afternoon surface analysis showed a front extending from central IN through central OH (north of KDAY and south of KMFD and KCAK) and into western PA (between KPIT and KBTP) to an area of low pressure near KDUJ. A warm front extended southeast from this low into northern MD (near or east of KHGR) to central DE (between KDOV and KGED). Ongoing strong diabatic heating across the warm sector has resulted in sufficient weakening of surface-based CINH per modified PIT 12Z sounding with current surface conditions. This has resulted in the development of an extensive cumulus and moderate cumulus field across central and southeast OH into western and southwest PA. Boundary layer moistening combined with the strong heating and steepening lapse rates will support further destabilization with MUCAPE already ranging from 1500-2000 J/kg. Timing of an MCV, currently located in west-central OH, suggests an increase in forcing for ascent with this feature will proceed into the OH and far western PA portion of the discussion area by 19-21Z. This will support thunderstorm development, while a favorable CAPE/shear environment (with 50-kt westerly winds at 3 km per wind data at PIT and CTP) favors primarily a linear storm mode, producing damaging winds.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Strong to severe storms are expected to move to the east-southeast into southeast Pennsylvania by 5-6 PM EDT and northern Maryland between 6-8 PM EDT. Damaging winds and hail should be the primary severe risks, though a tornado threat cannot be ruled out.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Earlier low-level stratus clouds have dissipated across southeast PA, far northeast MD and southern NJ allowing for stronger surface heating. This warming of the environment is supporting steepening lapse rates, while moisture advection per south- southwesterly low-level winds into the discussion area will result in further destabilization through the late afternoon from south to north. MUCAPE across MD and DE ranges from 1000-2000 J/kg. These improving thermodynamics for thunderstorm development combined with strong effective bulk shear of 40-50 kt already present across this region with the approach of a midlevel perturbation/MCV will likely allow storms to remain strong-severe as they advance from eastern parts of WW 84 into the discussion area.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Thunderstorm potential is increasing across central Indiana and west-central Ohio. Primary severe threats will be strong, gusty winds and hail. Area will be monitored for a potential severe thunderstorm watch.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Recent satellite imagery shows increasing vertical development with the cumulus clouds across central Indiana. This area is on the northern edge of the warm, moist air and downstream of an approaching mesoscale convective vortex (MCV), which is located across central Illinois. As the MCV continues to move east-southeast this afternoon, localized ascent will overspread the warm, moist airmass across central Indiana and west-central Ohio. This increasing ascent should be enough to lift/cool the remaining capping inversion and allow thunderstorms to develop. Lapse rates across the area are in the 7-8 C/km range and would support an isolated hail threat with initial discrete cells. However, if thunderstorm coverage increases as inhibition weakens, potential upscale growth into a complex of thunderstorms may yield a transition to more of a damaging wind threat. The area will continue to be monitored for a potential severe thunderstorm watch.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Isolated strong to severe wind gusts and perhaps some hail will be possible through this evening. Watch issuance is not expected.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Weak convergence along a surface dryline and subtle large-scale lift associated with a low-amplitude mid-level shortwave trough ejecting northeastward over the southern High Plains this afternoon should be sufficient to initiate at least isolated convection along the dryline over the next couple of hours. Recent visible satellite imagery shows increased mid-level cloudiness across west TX into the TX Panhandle. With temperatures east of the dryline reaching into the mid to upper 90s and greater low-level moisture in the eastern TX/OK Panhandles and far western OK, MLCAPE has increased into the 1000-2000 J/kg range. Mid-level flow is modestly stronger across the TX/OK Panhandles, and weakens quickly with southward extent into west TX. In addition, upper-level winds will remain weak across this area. Still, a deeply mixed boundary layer with very steep (8-9 degree C/km) low and mid-level lapse rates should enhance convective downdrafts. Isolated strong to severe winds appear to be the main threat, although some hail may occur with the strongest thunderstorms. Overall, thunderstorm coverage will likely remain too isolated to justify watch issuance.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe storms producing damaging wind and hail persist across much of WW 84 late this afternoon. Northern portions of this watch should be able to be cleared first, though storms currently moving into the northwest part of WW 84 preclude any clearing of counties at this time.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Trends in mosaic radar imagery showed a leading broken band of storms extending from south-central PA (Huntingdon County) to central OH (Muskingum County). Some of these storms have been severe, thus far, producing large hail and damaging winds. Forcing for ascent attendant to a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) will continue to advance from eastern OH through southern PA and northern MD through this evening. This combined with moderate instability and strong effective bulk shear along and south of the leading band of storms will support a continued severe weather threat with the stronger storms. Meanwhile, a second shorter band of storms was located from northern Beaver County, PA to Holmes County, OH, with this activity appearing to be co-located with the MCV. The Beaver County storm was moving to the east at 45 kt and could pose a severe threat. However, this activity may be slightly elevated as it is located north of a wind shift. Locally strong winds and/or hail cannot be ruled out, though the overall severe threat across the far northwest to north-central part of WW 84 may be diminishing. ..Peters.. 05/12/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will spread southeast across ww85 over the next several hours. Hail/wind are the primary threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Remnant MCV from early-morning convection over northern IN has moved east-southeast into central PA where it appears to be partly responsible for aiding renewed thunderstorm development. Over the last 1-2 hours a corridor of upward-evolving convection has organized across southern PA and this activity is spreading/developing east-southeast across central portions of ww85. Radar/observational data suggests this activity is generating outflow that is surging well ahead of the convection but new thunderstorms may ultimately develop near the outflow/synoptic front intersection in the vicinity of Baltimore. Primary tornado threat will be with any supercells that evolve across eastern MD, utilizing aforementioned boundary where low-level helicity is maximized. Otherwise, hail/wind are the primary threats. ..Darrow.. 05/12/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: Severe threat will sag southeast across the Delmarva region this evening. Strong winds and hail are the primary threats.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: Loosely organized squall line has developed across the Delmarva region this evening. This MCS is shifting east-southeast and will primarily affect southern DE into southeast MD over the next 1-2 hours. Several embedded updrafts exhibit large hail characteristics and damaging winds should also accompany this activity. Severe threat will shift off the MD coast later this evening. ..Darrow.. 05/13/2018 ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...
